reading: Joined by the term Products, a reading: BigCommerce's Catalog API, which 'manages products, categories, brands, bulk pricing rules, and more' (BC-S-0017), and its scope store_v2_products, 'View and modify products' (BC-S-0021), name the same object as Shopify's Products (SH-S-1509), Salla's Merchant API folder Products (SA-S-1022), WooCommerce's Products menu (WC-S-0049) and Zid's Products > Managing Products (ZD-S-0914). Like SH-C-020, WC-C-064 and ZD-C-083, BC-C-001 is coarse: Q1 put in it the API groups Catalog - Product variants, Product variant options and Product modifiers (BC-I-0021 to BC-I-0023), which CM-CAT-002 holds, so it lands in the parent CM-CAT-001. Strained by the dry run's rule S1 only: one of its statements, that files are added to digital products via the control panel (BC-S-0023), is cited in CM-SEL-002, another tree; the concern itself is the catalog, and no part of it is a digital product's own concern.

Joined by the term Brands, a reading: BigCommerce's Catalog brands endpoints, which 'create individual brands and modify the brands associated with a store's products' (BC-S-0024), are Salla's Merchant API folder Brands (SA-S-1056) and WooCommerce's Products > Brands (WC-S-0054): in each a brand is an object a product is associated with. Zid's Product Brands is an API group named only (ZD-I-0010, in CM-CAT-005's Zid cell).

Joined by the term Categories, a reading: BigCommerce's Catalog categories (BC-S-0026) are Salla's Merchant API folder Categories (SA-S-1053), WooCommerce's Products > Categories (WC-S-0052) and Zid's Product Categories (ZD-S-0009); Shopify's Collections are in the capability by the anchor's join on role. Category trees aren't a capability of their own: BigCommerce calls its category trees and their categories endpoints 'the more modern and performant counterparts to the categories (deprecated) endpoints' (BC-S-0027), the same object through a newer API.

Joined by the term Inventory, a reading: BigCommerce's Inventory API, 'location-aware, item-level inventory data' (BC-S-0030), and its scope store_inventory, 'View and modify store inventory' (BC-S-0034), are Shopify's admin navigation item Inventory (SH-S-1511), Salla's Inventory management (SA-S-1797), WooCommerce's Products > Inventory settings (WC-S-0013) and Zid's Inventory Management / إدارة المخزون plan line (ZD-S-0918): the stock quantities of products. BigCommerce's own concern splits its locations off (BC-C-005), as the model does (CM-INV-005).

Joined by the terms Locations and Inventory locations, a reading: BigCommerce's Locations, which 'allow merchants to track product inventory across multiple physical or virtual locations' (BC-S-0037), and its plan line Inventory locations (BC-S-0038) are Shopify's Locations (SH-S-1493) and its plan row Inventory locations (SH-S-7010), and Zid's Create Location in its Inventories group (ZD-S-0023). Salla's branches and warehouses are in the capability by the anchor's join on role.

Joined by the term Pricing, a reading: BigCommerce's Pricing API, 'Get product pricing on BigCommerce-hosted storefronts' (BC-S-0053), the price of a product, which Salla's webhook product.price.updated names (SA-S-1599) and WooCommerce's Marketplace category Pricing names without saying what it holds (WC-S-0735). Strained: no platform defines CM-CAT-013, and what its other cells show is setting a product's price (Salla's Automatic pricing, Zid's Custom Product Pricing) or apps for it; BigCommerce's Pricing API reads prices for a storefront, with no scopes, through CORS (BC-S-0054). Whether reading a storefront's prices and setting them are one capability isn't stated. The API group is a place of its own (BC-I-0049), so a reviewer may split it into a capability. Price lists, which set prices for customer groups, are BC-C-007, domain D.
